counterfactual.change: changed dt from 0.031907211696269457 to 0.001 (single field); smaller displacement per step/substep allows collision to be detected, so no_tunneling violation disappears while keeping steps=1

explanation: Body 0 starts just east of thin wall 0 (x=[5.5,5.7], distance 0.1) with high speed 55.6 and dt=0.0319. In one step it displaces ~1.06 west and ~1.43 south to x=5.24 west of wall, crossing straight through the wall interior between discrete positions. Despite 60 substeps, there is no continuous collision detection for thin walls, so the engine misses the wall crossing and reports tunneling at step 1. Reducing dt to 0.001 removes the tunneling, confirming large displacement per (sub)step vs wall thickness is the cause.

violation.detail: body centre moved through wall 0 between steps 0 and 1

vision_note: In step 0 the red body is just to the east of the thin vertical wall at mid-height. In step 1 it has jumped far south to the bottom tip of the wall where it overlaps the wall, implying its centre crossed straight through the wall interior between the two discrete frames.
